channel.title: RAM recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Ram 1500 Rear Seat Belt Anchor Problem
item.description: Certain Ram 1500 trucks may have a problem with the seat belt buckles in the second row. The anchors that attach the center and left-side seat belt buckles to the vehicle may not have been installed correctly. Because of this, these seat belts may not properly hold occupants in place during a crash, which increases the risk of injury. These vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for seat belt anchorages.

item.title: Ram Trucks Instrument Panel Display Failure
item.description: On certain 2025-2026 Ram pickup and cab chassis models, a software error may cause the instrument panel display to fail.

item.title: Jeep And Ram Trailer Tow Module Failure
item.description: On these Jeep Wagoneer S, Ram, and Jeep Cherokee vehicles, the trailer tow module was not designed correctly. Because of this, the lights on a trailer you're towing may fail to come on, and the trailer's brakes may not work.

item.title: Ram 3500, 5500 trucks: airbag and stability flaw
item.description: Some 2025 Ram pickup and cab chassis trucks, including 3500 and 5500 models, may have a software error in the module that controls the air bags and seat belts. Because of this software error, the driver's side air bag and seat belt pretensioner may fail to work in a crash, and the electronic stability control system may be turned off.

item.title: Wheelchair Restraints in Various Vehicles May Not Lock
item.description: Certain vehicles equipped with QRT-Deluxe or QRT-Max wheelchair restraints may have retractors that fail to lock. If the retractor does not lock, a wheelchair inside the vehicle may not be properly secured.

item.title: Ram 1500, 2500 and 3500 side airbag inflators may rupture
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Ram 1500 Classic, Ram 2500, and Ram 3500 vehicles because of a manufacturing defect in the side curtain airbags. The part that fills the airbag with gas, on the right side, the left side, or both, may break apart. A dealer will replace one or both of the side curtain airbags as needed, at no cost to the owner. Chrysler mailed notification letters to owners, and the company has a customer service line for owners with questions.

item.title: Ram 3500, 5500 Instrument Cluster Display Failure
item.description: A software error can cause the instrument panel display in your truck to go blank. This means important information, like warning lights or which gear you're in, may not show up when you need it. Dealers will inspect your vehicle and update the instrument panel software, or replace the instrument panel cluster if that's needed, free of charge. Owner notification letters have already been mailed to affected owners.

item.title: Ram Trucks: Driver's Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: Certain Ram 1500, 2500, 3500, 4500, and 5500 trucks have a problem with the steering column control module that can stop the driver's side air bag from deploying properly in a crash. The air bag is meant to help protect the driver, but this issue means it may not inflate the way it's supposed to when it's needed, which could affect how well the driver is protected during a collision.

item.title: Ram ProMaster Radiator Fan Circuit May Overheat
item.description: The electrical circuit that powers the radiator cooling fan in these Ram ProMaster vans may overheat. An electrical circuit that gets too hot increases the chance of a fire starting in the vehicle. Because of this safety risk, some owners have already been sent an early notification letter ahead of the full recall notice, telling them about the danger before the repair is ready. Chrysler will fix the affected fan system as part of this recall.

item.title: Ram ProMaster Electric Vehicles Can Lose Drive Power
item.description: Some Ram ProMaster battery electric vehicles have software in the electric drive module that may not manage torque correctly. This can cause the vehicle to lose drive power.

item.title: RAM 1500, 2500, 3500 Side Airbag Inflators May Rupture
item.description: The side curtain airbags on the left and right sides of these trucks have inflators that were manufactured with a defect. Because of this defect, the inflator can rupture when the airbag deploys. If that happens, small sharp pieces of metal can fly out with enough force to strike people inside the vehicle, which can cause injury to the driver or passengers nearby.

item.title: Ram ProMaster, Dodge Journey backup camera may fail
item.description: Cracks can develop in a microprocessor used by the rearview camera on these vehicles. When that happens, the camera's image may not display properly on the screen, so these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard for rear visibility. Dealers will replace the rearview camera at no charge, though the replacement parts are not yet available. Interim letters warning owners of the issue were mailed starting September 30, 2025, and a second letter announcing the final remedy is expected around July 2026.

item.title: Ram Trucks May Show Wrong Brake Warning Light
item.description: On some Ram 3500, 2500, 4500, and 5500 trucks, the instrument panel display may show the wrong warning light for the brake system. Because the light can be incorrect, it may not properly alert the driver to an important safety problem with the truck. Failing to warn the driver about a real issue increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Ram ProMaster Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: Some Ram ProMaster vans have a software error in the security gateway module that can cause the rearview camera image to not display at all. This means the driver may not be able to see the view behind the vehicle when backing up. Dealers will update the security gateway module software to fix this, at no cost to owners. Chrysler has already begun mailing notification letters to owners about this issue.

item.title: Ram Heavy-Duty Trucks May Show Wrong Gear
item.description: Certain Ram 2500 and 3500 trucks with a 3.5-inch instrument cluster and column shifter have a software error that can make the gear selection display show the wrong gear. This could mislead the driver about which gear is actually selected.

item.title: Ram 1500 Driver Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: On certain 2019-2024 Ram 1500 trucks, the air bag on the driver's side may not be properly connected. Because of this loose connection, if the vehicle is in a crash, the air bag might not inflate the way it is supposed to.

item.title: Ram Trucks Side Airbag Inflator Can Rupture
item.description: On these Ram trucks, the right and left side curtain air bag inflators may rupture due to a manufacturing defect.

item.title: Ram Trucks Brake Control Unit May Fail
item.description: Some Ram 2500, 3500, 4500, and 5500 trucks have a hydraulic control unit that may fail. If it fails, the anti-lock brakes, electronic stability control, and traction control systems can stop working. Losing these systems can make the vehicle harder to control and increases the risk of a crash.

item.title: Ram 1500 Tow Mirror Glass Can Fall Off
item.description: Chrysler (FCA US) is recalling certain Ram 1500 Classic pickup trucks equipped with heated trailer tow rearview mirrors. The glass in the driver's side mirror can come loose and detach from the mirror housing. Because the mirror glass may fall off, the driver may not be able to see clearly out of that mirror while driving.

item.title: Ram 1500 Software Can Shut Off Stability Control
item.description: Certain Ram 1500 trucks have a software problem in the computer that runs the anti-lock brakes. Because of the fault, that computer can shut off the truck's electronic stability control system. With stability control switched off, the truck no longer meets the federal safety standard that covers these systems. The fix is a software update for the brake control computer, done by a dealer at no charge to the owner.

item.title: Chrysler, Jeep, Ram Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: A software issue in the radio can prevent the rearview camera image from displaying on the screen. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet the requirements of the federal safety standard for rear visibility, FMVSS 111. To fix the problem, dealers will update the radio software, or the software update will be delivered over-the-air. This repair is free of charge for owners of the affected vehicles.

item.title: RAM Trucks Transmission Leak Can Cut Power
item.description: Some 2023 Ram 1500, 2500, and 3500 trucks have a transmission control unit with a weld that may not be strong enough. This can allow transmission fluid to leak onto the electrical components inside the unit. If that happens, the truck can lose the ability to drive under power, or it may not properly hold in the park position.

item.title: Ram ProMaster Missing Side Door Safety Beam
item.description: Some ProMaster vans are missing a beam inside the side door meant to help protect occupants in a side-impact crash. These vans also have a tire placard listing the wrong seating capacity, which could lead to the vehicle carrying more people than it should.

item.title: Dodge Durango, Ram Trucks Lose Stability Control
item.description: A software problem in the ABS control module can disable the electronic stability control system on affected Dodge Durango and Ram trucks. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for electronic stability control systems.

item.title: Ram ProMaster Electronic Stability Control Malfunction
item.description: An electrical ground connection in these ProMaster vans may not be secure. If the connection is loose, the electronic stability control system may stop working.

item.title: Jeep, Ram, Chrysler Air Bag May Not Deploy
item.description: Certain Jeep, Ram, and Chrysler vehicles may have a steering column control module that wasn't welded correctly. Because of this welding problem, the driver's air bag may not deploy during a crash the way it is supposed to. This affects a range of trucks and SUVs, including the Wrangler, Grand Cherokee, Gladiator, Wagoneer, Grand Wagoneer, Pacifica, and Voyager, meaning the driver may not get the protection the air bag is meant to provide.

item.title: Ram ProMaster left taillight and turn signal may fail
item.description: In these Ram ProMaster vans, a wiring connection may be poor, which can stop the left taillight and the left turn signal from working. When that happens, the left rear light does not come on and the left turn signal does not flash, so other drivers get no signal that the van is turning and have a harder time seeing it. Because of this, the vans do not meet the federal rule covering lamps, reflective devices and related equipment.

item.title: Ram ProMaster driver seat belt warning may not work
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Ram ProMaster vans. The warning light and chime that remind the driver to buckle up may not turn on the way they are supposed to. Because of this, these vans do not meet the federal safety rule covering occupant crash protection. Dealers will look at the driver's seat belt buckle and replace it if needed.

item.title: Ram truck light controls may swap signals and high beams
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Ram trucks. The control module in the steering column can mix up the light controls: using the turn signal may switch on the high beams, and using the high beams may switch on a turn signal. The turn signal may also fail to shut itself off after a turn. Because of this, these trucks do not meet the federal safety standard for lamps and reflective equipment. Dealers will update the module's software and replace the module if needed.

item.title: Ram trucks may not show the rearview camera image
item.description: The radio software in these trucks can stop the rearview camera picture from appearing on the screen. Federal safety rules require these vehicles to provide a rear view image, and with this software problem they do not meet that requirement. Chrysler is recalling certain 2022-2023 Ram 1500 and Ram 3500 Cab Chassis rated under 10,000 pounds, along with 2022-2024 Ram 2500 trucks. Dealers will load corrected radio software at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Jeep and RAM Diesel Engines May Stall
item.description: On some Jeep Grand Cherokee and RAM 1500 trucks with 3.0L diesel engines, a sensor on the crankshaft may come apart. This can cause the engine to lose track of fuel injector and camshaft timing, which may make the engine stall.

item.title: Ram ProMaster Park Gear May Not Engage
item.description: On certain ProMaster vans with a 62TE transmission, debris inside the transmission may keep the park pawl from fully engaging the park gear.

item.title: Ram 1500 Software Glitch May Stall Engine
item.description: Some 2021 Ram 1500 trucks with the 5.7-liter eTorque engine have a computer chip, called the powertrain control module, that controls the engine. A software problem in this chip can cause the engine to get the wrong mixture of fuel and air. This incorrect fuel mixture can cause the engine to stall while you are driving.

item.title: Ram 1500 Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Ram 1500 and Ram 2500 trucks because a part called the trailer reverse steering control module may stop the rearview camera image from appearing on the screen when the truck is shifted into reverse. Because the rearview image does not always show up, these vehicles do not meet a federal safety rule that requires vehicles to give the driver a view of what is behind them while backing up.

item.title: Ram Diesel Trucks Heater Relay Fire Risk
item.description: Some Ram trucks with a Cummins diesel engine have a heater relay that may develop an electrical short, whether the ignition is on or off. This short can cause a fire in the engine compartment, increasing the risk of injury.

item.title: Ram ProMaster Rearview Camera Is Wrong Type
item.description: Some Ram ProMaster Chassis Cab and incomplete vehicles were built with an analog rearview camera, which is the wrong type for this vehicle and cannot be properly installed. Because of this, these vehicles do not meet federal safety rules that require a working rearview camera. Without the correct camera, the driver may not get a proper rearview image when backing up, which can reduce how well they can see behind the vehicle.

item.title: Ram pickup tailgates may open while driving
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Ram 1500, 2500 and 3500 pickup trucks. The strikers that the tailgate latches onto may be out of alignment, so the tailgate may not latch properly. A tailgate that is not latched can open while the truck is being driven. Dealers will inspect how the tailgate striker lines up with the latch on the truck bed and adjust it if needed, free of charge. Chrysler mailed owner letters on December 22, 2022.

item.title: Ram 2500 and 3500 Transmission Fluid Leak
item.description: On certain Ram 2500 and 3500 trucks, a build-up of pressure and heat inside the transmission may cause transmission fluid to leak out through the dipstick tube.

item.title: Jeep and Ram Diesel Fuel Pump Can Stall Engine
item.description: On these Jeep and Ram vehicles with 3.0-liter diesel engines, the high pressure fuel pump may fail. If this happens, the engine can stall.

item.title: Ram 4500, 5500 Rear Brake Hose May Rupture
item.description: On some Ram 4500 and 5500 Cab Chassis trucks, the inside diameter of the rear brake hose may be too small. Because of this, the hose could rupture. These vehicles do not meet federal safety standards for brake hoses. If a hose ruptures, the vehicle can lose its ability to brake properly, which increases the risk of a crash while driving.
